name: Dactyl
summary: Dactyl trained an LSTM policy with PPO across a massively randomized simulation, then deployed it on a Shadow Dexterous Hand to reorient a cube using vision and touch. It never saw the real world during training. The policy rediscovered human-recognizable grasp strategies such as finger pivoting and sliding, and the follow-up work solved a Rubik's cube one-handed with automatic domain randomization.
innovation: Domain randomization at extreme scale as the sole sim-to-real mechanism.
Recurrent policies that infer unobserved physical parameters online, an implicit system identification.
matters: The canonical demonstration that dexterity can be learned in simulation and shipped to hardware.
limits: Thousands of years of simulated experience for one narrow task; brittle outside the randomization distribution.
lineage: PPO plus domain randomization pushed to its limit on a high-DoF hand.
